newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ahold sees significant EPS growth.
newsitem.headline: Ahold sees significant EPS growth.

text.p: Dutch supermarkets group Koninklijke Ahold NV said on Thursday it expected earnings per share to grow significantly in 1997.
"The consolidated result after taxes will be considerably higher in 1997 than in 1996. Earnings per share will also show significant growth in 1997," the company said in statement.
It added that it also expected a rise of shareholders' equity and solvency rates.

Ahold said both sales and operating results were seen growing this year in the Netherlands and other European countries. In the U.S., sales and operating results will rise significantly, primarily due to the full-year consolidation of subsidiary Stop & Shop.

The 50 percent owned Brazilian unit Bompreco will make a positive contribution this year to operating results and net earnings but Ahold expects further unspecified start-up losses at its Asia Pacific operations.
Ahold earlier reported 1996 net profits had surged by 39 percent to 632.4 million guilders and net earnings per share grew by 16.7 percent to 4.30 guilders.
"The growth in net earnings was mainly attributable to considerably higher operating results," it said.
Group sales went up by 23.4 percent to 36.5 billion guilders. Excluding the effect of last year's takeover of Stop & Shop in the U.S. sales rose by about 11 percent.
Ahold said sales in the Netherlands grew by 4.4 percent to 15 billion guilders but turnover in other European countries showed a hefty 33 percent rise to 2.5 billion.
Sales in the U.S. grew by 34.9 percent to $11.2 billion. Excluding Stop & Shop's sales, last year's U.S. turnover increase was 8.7 percent.
It said this included the loss of sales from stores of its U.S. unit Edwards which were sold to satisfy anti-trust regulations.
In the course of 1996, Ahold launched supermarket activities in Singapore, Malaysia and China with local partners. The 1996 sales in this region remained limited to 55.9 million guilders.
